observations.statement: The window declares seglog authoritative while redb, JSONL, and Tantivy are derived stores maintained by projectors.
Remote regex-index operation combines local bare-clone caches, local dirty staging, periodic re-anchoring, and cache eviction.
Regex snapshots use generation directories, mmap-backed lookup state, Roaring postings, and an atomically swapped in-process snapshot.
Seglog records use a payload CRC32, optional LZ4 compression, deterministic segment names, and checkpoint-based replay.
The EventRecord section explicitly limits its closure claim to the envelope and acknowledges that concrete payload families and other storage value families remain incomplete.

candidate_findings.title: Local regex-index location contradicts repository-exclusion claims
candidate_findings.claim: Within the window, local regex storage is located relative to the project root at `.puppet-master/project/state/regex_index/`, while the prose simultaneously says the index is not inside the repository/Git working tree and therefore needs no ignore rule. No alternate out-of-tree local-project root or Git exclusion mechanism resolves the contradiction.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Implementations can choose incompatible roots, expose large generated state in Git status, recursively index managed data, or apply cleanup and permissions to the wrong location.

candidate_findings.title: Short hash cache namespaces lack collision handling
candidate_findings.claim: Remote project and submodule cache ownership is keyed by only the first eight hexadecimal characters of non-cryptographic xxh3, but the window defines no collision detection, alternate suffix, namespace allocation, or refusal rule. A manifest mapping does not explain how two full identities sharing one `hash8` receive distinct directories.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A collision can mix repositories, dirty state, indexes, credentials-adjacent metadata, or eviction targets across projects, violating project isolation and risking destructive cleanup.

candidate_findings.title: Pending-sync remote state is not durably protected from crash or eviction
candidate_findings.claim: Dirty remote buffers remain local pending-sync state under the remote cache, while generation and deleted metadata are held in an in-memory `RwLock` and `index_meta.json` explicitly omits dirty-layer state. Cache eviction has no stated pending-sync exclusion, durable duplicate, flush handshake, or recovery rule.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A crash, restart, manual clear, or disk-pressure eviction can lose or misclassify unsynchronized user edits, clear the wrong generation, or resurrect deleted files.

candidate_findings.title: Frequency table is outside snapshot integrity and publication boundaries
candidate_findings.claim: `frequency_table.bin` sits outside generation directories, is omitted from `index_meta.json` checksums, and is not listed among the objects held by the atomically published `IndexSnapshot`, even though build and query logic share it and incremental builds reuse it.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A crash, corruption, or concurrent full rebuild can pair postings generated with one frequency table with queries using another, producing false negatives that downstream ripgrep verification cannot recover because omitted candidates are never verified.

candidate_findings.title: Case-collision handling deliberately drops searchable files
candidate_findings.claim: On case-insensitive filesystems, enumeration keeps only the first case-colliding path and merely logs later collisions, while line-level verification runs only on candidate file IDs. No fail-closed, degraded-result, alternate identity, or exhaustive fallback is defined.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A valid repository containing case-distinct paths can produce silent search false negatives while the UI may still present results as authoritative.

candidate_findings.title: Submodule clone ownership has two unreconciled directory shapes
candidate_findings.claim: The window alternates between `git/m/{sub_hash8}/` and `git/modules/{submodule_path}/` as storage for separately bare-cloned submodules without defining whether these are aliases, separate layers, or migration forms, or which path owns fetch, lookup, cleanup, and recovery.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Independent implementers can write and read different locations, orphan large clones, fail cleanup, or verify a gitlink against the wrong repository.

candidate_findings.title: Seglog framing cannot safely resynchronize after header corruption
candidate_findings.claim: The stream is called length-prefixed, but the concrete header contains variable-shaped fields and only `payload_length`; the checksum covers stored payload bytes, not the header or an entire frame. No frame magic, encoded header length, header checksum, maximum length, or resynchronization algorithm is specified, yet corrupt records are required to be skipped.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: If header bytes or `payload_length` are damaged, a reader cannot reliably find the next record boundary. The mandated skip behavior can misparse arbitrary bytes as records or make recovery impossible for the canonical event source.

candidate_findings.title: Skipping a corrupt canonical event leaves an unmodeled causal hole
candidate_findings.claim: Corrupt records are skipped and projectors resume from a last-known-good checkpoint, but the window defines no halted/degraded projection state, durable gap marker, dependency invalidation, quarantine lane, operator decision, or rule for whether later records may project across the missing sequence.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Later events can depend on the skipped event. Continuing can materialize a plausible but false state across redb, JSONL, Tantivy, History, exports, and GUI projections.

candidate_findings.title: Canonical append durability and live-tail commit semantics are missing
candidate_findings.claim: The window specifies one record per append, one active segment, rotation triggers, and active-tail consumption, but not sequence allocation, writer exclusion, append acknowledgement, fsync cadence, directory sync, close/rename atomicity, or a reader-visible commit boundary. Partial-tail handling is defined only for restart recovery.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Concurrent writers or a crash after an acknowledged append can create duplicate sequences, lost events, premature corruption handling, or readers observing a partially written live record in the authoritative store.

candidate_findings.title: Projector checkpoint commits are not coupled to derived-store updates
candidate_findings.claim: Replay starts from one committed checkpoint while projectors update redb, JSONL, and Tantivy, but the window does not define per-projector checkpoints, transaction ordering, two-phase publication, rollback, or idempotent update keys for all three stores.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A crash between a derived write and checkpoint commit can duplicate output on replay; a checkpoint committed before all stores update can permanently omit projections. The stores can then disagree about the same canonical sequence.

candidate_findings.title: Duplicated header and EventRecord fields have no consistency rule
candidate_findings.claim: The seglog header may duplicate event type, sequence, timestamps, and payload length while the decoded EventRecord is semantic authority, and physical replay identity also includes sequence. No rule requires equality, identifies which copy drives scanning and ordering, or defines quarantine for a checksum-valid mismatch.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A valid-payload record with inconsistent header metadata can be routed, ordered, deduplicated, or recovered differently depending on which layer reads it.

candidate_findings.title: Idempotency scope and conflicting-duplicate behavior are undefined
candidate_findings.claim: `project_id` is optional in the physical header, but the proposed lookup key requires it. Duplicate delivery matches on `event_id` or `idempotency_key` according to an unspecified policy, with no namespace, retention lifetime, atomic reservation, or rule for the same key arriving with different payload bytes or schema versions.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Global events may be unindexable, distinct events may collapse across scopes, and concurrent conflicting appends may each appear accepted or silently return an unrelated original result.

candidate_findings.title: Compressed payload decoding has no resource or codec bounds
candidate_findings.claim: The header allows LZ4 and validates only stored payload length and CRC before decode. The window does not specify an uncompressed length, decompressed-size or ratio cap, codec framing/profile, allocation limit, timeout, or malformed-stream disposition.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A checksum-valid compressed payload can trigger excessive allocation or CPU use, and different codec interpretations can make replay nondeterministic across implementations.

candidate_findings.title: No-secret policy lacks an enforceable cross-store boundary
candidate_findings.claim: The window says EventRecord content must not contain secrets, but does not name the validating component, scan/redaction oracle, fail-closed result, quarantine behavior, or remediation for previously persisted values. The rule is scoped to EventRecord even though clone commands, SSH topology, URLs, caches, blobs, mirrors, and indexes are also persisted or generated.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Sensitive credential paths, command options, source content, or payload values can enter non-EventRecord stores or diagnostics and remain searchable, exported, backed up, or retained without a defined purge path.

candidate_findings.title: Retention and legal-hold mechanics are deferred rather than specified
candidate_findings.claim: Closed canonical segments are retained or migrated through a referenced governed retention/legal-hold policy, but this window defines no retention classes, hold authority, deletion eligibility, successor verification, compaction manifest, garbage-collection algorithm, user erasure behavior, or recovery test oracle.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Storage growth, compliance deletion, forensic preservation, and replay completeness cannot be implemented or tested deterministically from the stated boundary.

candidate_findings.title: Scale and latency claims have no reproducible acceptance oracle
candidate_findings.claim: The window gives precise index-size, write-time, and RSS expectations for repositories up to 50 GB but does not bind them to hardware profiles, source corpora, cold versus warm cache state, concurrency, percentile thresholds, measurement tooling, or pass/fail criteria.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The implementation can miss user-visible performance targets while still claiming conformance, and the stated estimates cannot reliably drive capacity, eviction, or fallback decisions.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: Generation-local file IDs are explicitly prohibited from being treated as stable across builds or snapshots.
xxh3 n-gram collisions are explicitly unioned into broader candidate sets, and ripgrep verification is retained for line-level correctness.
Dirty entries created after a re-anchor build starts are explicitly preserved by monotonically increasing generations.
The window supplies an in-process atomic snapshot swap and flushes new generation files before publication.
Unsupported EventRecord schema identifiers or versions are rejected rather than inferred, and missing concrete payload schemas are expressly treated as incomplete.
Seglog is explicitly identified as the authoritative EventRecord store, while redb event indexes are rebuildable pointers rather than a second mutable event source.
The section explicitly avoids overclaiming closure for runtime, GUI, security, and other unmaterialized value families.

unknowns.statement: Whether Puppet Master guarantees a single process and single writer for each storage or cache root is unknown.
unknowns.reason_unresolved: The bounded excerpt describes in-process locks and Arc lifetimes but contains no process-ownership contract.

unknowns.statement: Whether pending-sync remote editor buffers are durably duplicated outside the remote cache is unknown.
unknowns.reason_unresolved: The excerpt identifies them as local pending-sync state but does not name another durable store or recovery source.

unknowns.statement: Whether `git/m/{sub_hash8}` and `git/modules/{submodule_path}` are intentional separate layers is unknown.
unknowns.reason_unresolved: Both are described as locations for bare-cloned submodules without a relationship or precedence rule in the bounded excerpt.

unknowns.statement: Whether a concrete retention, legal-hold, and erasure contract exists outside this capsule is unknown.
unknowns.reason_unresolved: The excerpt invokes a governed policy but does not identify or materialize its authority and mechanics.

exact_evidence_refs.excerpt: Storage for the rewrite follows a multi-store design: **seglog** as the canonical append-only event stream, **redb** for durable KV state (settings, sessions, runs, checkpoints, editor state, analytics rollups), and **Tantivy** for full-text search. Projectors consume seglog and maintain a JSONL mirror, Tantivy indices, and redb state. Analytics scan jobs compute rollups from seglog and store them in redb for fast dashboard and Usage queries. This plan specifies **how** we implement it: file locations, event format, redb schema, projector behavior, and how we address gaps, failure modes, and optional enhancements.

All storage lives under a single **app data root** (for example `~/.puppet-master/`, `$XDG_DATA_HOME/puppet-master/`, `%APPDATA%/puppet-master`, or `~/Library/Application Support/puppet-master`). Project-scoped runtime state still lives under `.puppet-master/` inside the workspace when the feature is inherently project-local.

Regex-index storage policy: `regex_index/` lives under `.puppet-master/` managed state, not inside the user's repo/Git working tree, so no separate gitignore rule is required for ordinary project Git state. Regex-index directories use OS-specific indexer exclusions: Windows applies `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NOT_CONTENT_INDEXED` via `SetFileAttributesW`, macOS creates `.metadata_never_index` using the Spotlight convention, and Linux needs no default system-indexer marker. These exclusions prevent Spotlight/Defender I/O contention and file locks during builds.

| Path (relative to project root) | Purpose |
|----------------------------------|---------|
| `.puppet-master/project/state/regex_index/` | Root directory for the per-project sparse n-gram index |

Regex-index n-gram hashing uses xxHash (`xxh3`) through the `xxhash-rust` crate as the 64-bit hash function for n-gram keys. Classification: Non-cryptographic. Rationale: Fast with excellent distribution for index-key hashing, not security-sensitive hashing.

Remote Git regex-index cache policy: on remote project open, PM stores the local Git cache under `.puppet-master/cache/r/{hash8}/git/`, with remote submodules under `.puppet-master/cache/r/{hash8}/git/m/{sub_hash8}/` and submodule repositories under `git/modules/{submodule_path}/`. Clone mode may be full, shallow, or partial (`/shallow/partial`), but bare-clones are the storage shape: PM may run `git clone --bare ssh://remote_host/path/to/repo` or `git -c core.sshCommand="ssh -J remote_host" clone --bare`, where `core.sshCommand`, `remote_host`, `//remote_host/path/to/repo`, and remote `URL` handling are recorded for reproducibility. If auth or `/network` topology means the repository is only reachable from the remote host, PM initiates the clone remotely and streams a `git bundle` over SSH; if that fails, it falls back to the non-Git remote path.

Remote submodule and verification policy: CRITICAL FIX for bare-clone and recurse-submodules behavior is that `--recurse-submodules` is ignored with `--bare`, so PM parses `.gitmodules`/gitmodules, separately bare-clones each submodule repo after validating submodule paths, stores them under `git/modules/{submodule_path}/`, and includes `/modules/{submodule_path}/` content by reading the gitlink-referenced commit via `git show`. Bare Git clones cannot be searched directly by ripgrep; CRITICAL FIX verification resolves `file_id -> path`, runs `git show {anchor_sha}:{path}` / `git show {anchor}:{path}` / `git show {sha}:{path}` and pipes that content to ripgrep, while index-build bulk content reads use `git cat-file --batch`.

During bare-clone index builds that enumerate files with `git ls-tree` / `ls-tree`, PM detects case-insensitive filesystems, deduplicates entries by lowercased path, keeps the first entry encountered, and logs a `case-collisions` warning when later entries collapse to the same normalized path.

Remote dirty-file locality and re-anchor policy: dirty remote content is staged locally at `.puppet-master/cache/r/{hash8}/dirty/{relative_path}` so ripgrep can verify dirty files from local storage and keep the near-zero-SSH-during-grep guarantee. Content arrives with the file-change notification for files up to 1 MB or through background prefetch for larger files; if grep outruns that prefetch, PM may block briefly and then fall back to SSH ripgrep for that file. This near-zero policy SUPERSEDES any absolute zero-SSH claim for >1 MB dirty files. The dirty staging area is merged into the next re-anchor build before clearing.

Remote editor/search storage treats `remote proxy`, SSHFS-style, and `SSHFS` access as capability profiles over one remote project identity, not separate path authorities. Each profile records whether file-watch is native, proxied, or polling-derived; stale or disconnected remote search snapshots are `/read-only` until refresh, while dirty remote buffers remain local pending-sync state until the effective destination confirms write success.

Dirty-layer generation clearing is a CRITICAL FIX: dirty-layer entries carry a monotonically increasing `generation: u64`; when a re-anchor build starts, PM records `build_generation`, and on build completion clears only entries with `generation <= build_generation` / `generation ≤ build_generation`. Entries added during the build (`generation > build_generation`) survive so a long-running build cannot lose files dirtied during that build.

Dirty-layer concurrency uses `RwLock<HashMap<PathBuf, DirtyEntry>>`. Each `DirtyEntry` carries the generation counter and deleted flag; PM-mediated writes take a brief write lock for synchronous inserts, file watcher inserts are async backup/dedup, and query readers clone the relevant dirty entries at query start.

Regex-index snapshot publication is a CRITICAL FIX: PM publishes `ArcSwap<Arc<IndexSnapshot>>` using the `arc-swap` crate. `IndexSnapshot` holds the mmap handle for `lookup.bin`, the postings file handle, `file_map` data, and `index_meta`; the builder constructs a new snapshot from `gen-{N+1}/` and performs one atomic pointer swap. Readers hold `Arc` references until query completion, old generation directories are cleaned only after the last reader exits, and the generation-directory design removes rename-of-mmap'd-file / d-file hazards on Windows and eliminates multi-file rename atomicity issues.

Regex-index durability before publish: all new generation files are flushed with `File::sync_all()` / `sync_all` before ArcSwap publication, preventing a crash-after-swap-before-flush from leaving truncated content behind valid filenames.
| `.puppet-master/project/state/regex_index/frequency_table.bin` | Project-specific blended frequency table (256x256 `u16`) used by both build and query |
| `.puppet-master/cache/r/{hash8}/` | Remote project cache root (`hash8` = first 8 chars of xxh3(project_id)) |
| `.puppet-master/cache/r/{hash8}/git/m/{sub_hash8}/` | Bare Git clones for submodules (recursive, max depth 5) |
| `.puppet-master/cache/r/{hash8}/dirty/` | Local staging area for remote dirty-file content used by verification and re-anchor merge |
| `.puppet-master/cache/r/{hash8}/manifest.json` | `hash8 -> project_id/submodule_path` mapping for recovery, MAX_PATH mitigation, and cleanup |

Remote cache eviction is storage-owned and does not run on ordinary project close. PM evicts remote project caches after 30 days of no project opens, when the total cache directory exceeds the global cache size limit (default: 50 GB or 10% of free disk at first cache creation, whichever is smaller), or when the user manually evicts one project cache or chooses Clear All Remote Caches. Disk-pressure eviction removes LRU project caches until the cache is under limit. Eviction deletes both the Git cache and regex index for that project; the next open performs a fresh clone plus background index build.

- **`file_map.bin`:** header `PMFM` + `schema_version:u32` + `entry_count:u32`. Entries are `path_byte_length:u32` + UTF-8 path bytes. Stored paths are forward-slash (`/`) normalized regardless of OS and convert to native separators only at query/I/O time, matching Git internal convention and keeping the `file_map` format platform-independent. File IDs are generation-local only and MUST NOT be treated as stable across builds or across snapshot generations.

- **`lookup.bin`:** header `PMLK` + `schema_version:u32` + `entry_count:u32`. Entries are sorted `(xxh3_hash:u64, postings_offset:u64)` pairs. `lookup.bin` remains a separate mmap file from offset 0; if a future packed format combines files, the lookup region MUST begin at a 64 KB-aligned offset for Windows `MapViewOfFile` compatibility. Startup validation checks both `12 + entry_count * 16` sizing and every referenced postings offset before mmap. When two distinct n-grams produce the same xxh3 64-bit hash, their posting lists are merged at index time (Roaring union); the lookup table has exactly one entry per unique hash. Collisions broaden candidates but never affect correctness.

- **`postings.bin`:** header `PMPL` + `schema_version:u32`. Entries are `bitmap_byte_length:u32` + portable-format Roaring Bitmap bytes produced with `RoaringBitmap::serialize_into` portable mode. Postings store `u32` file IDs only; line-level precision always comes from ripgrep verification on candidate files.

- **`index_meta.json`:** metadata object with these required fields: `anchor_sha: string | null`, `build_timestamp_utc: string`, `schema_version: u32`, `file_count: u32`, `generation: u64`, `checksums: { file_map, lookup, postings }`, `case_sensitive_fs: bool`, and `roaring_format: "portable"`. Dirty-layer state is NOT persisted in `index_meta.json`; it is reconstructed as needed because the index is a cache.

Incremental serialization remains full-snapshot I/O: even when extraction is incremental, PM rewrites `postings.bin`, `lookup.bin`, and `file_map.bin`, so write cost is `O(index_size)`. For a 50 GB repo with a roughly 2-5 GB index, expected storage time is about 1-3s on NVMe and 3-7s on SATA SSD; SSD storage is strongly recommended for repos above 5 GB, HDD performance is not targeted, and an append-only/log-structured (`/log-structured`) posting format is reserved for v2 if write amplification becomes a bottleneck.
- **Stability rule:** `frequency_table.bin` is shared by both build and query logic and is recomputed only on full rebuilds. Incremental rebuilds reuse the current stored table.

Sparse n-gram index is typically 1-10% of source code size: 50 MB source produces ~0.5-5 MB index, 500 MB → ~5-50 MB, 1 GB → ~50-100 MB, 50 GB → ~2-5 GB. Only the hash lookup table is mmap'd in process memory; the OS pages in what is needed per query. Peak RSS contribution is typically <500 MB even for large repositories.
Every seglog record MUST include a CRC32 checksum computed over the record payload. This is a mandatory correctness requirement, not an optional enhancement.

On read, CRC32 MUST be validated before the record is processed. If validation fails:
- the corrupt record is skipped
- PM emits a recovery/integrity event including record offset and expected vs observed CRC
- projectors resume from the last known-good checkpoint rather than replaying the corrupt record
Seglog uses a length-prefixed binary record stream. The canonical payload codec is MessagePack; mirrors and diagnostics may expose the same envelope in JSON, but JSON is not the on-disk authority.

version: u8,
  segment_generation: u32,
  event_type: string,
  sequence_id: u64,
  source_timestamp_ns?: u64,
  observed_timestamp_ns: u64,
  session_id?: string,
  project_id?: string,
  payload_length: u32,
  checksum_crc32: u32,
  compression: "none" | "lz4"
}

Wire-format rules:
- `payload` is the encoded event payload after any payload-only compression step.
- `checksum_crc32` is computed over the stored payload bytes.
- readers validate `payload_length`, then checksum, then decode.
- a single append operation produces exactly one record; record order is the canonical event order.
- `source_timestamp_ns?` preserves upstream/authored time when the source provides it; `observed_timestamp_ns` is always populated by the seglog writer.

Rules:
- there is exactly one active writable segment per seglog generation
- active segment path: `storage/seglog/seg-{generation:06}-{start_seq:020}.active`
- closed segment path: `storage/seglog/seg-{generation:06}-{start_seq:020}-{end_seq:020}.seglog`
- rotate on size threshold, clean shutdown, explicit maintenance, or schema-generation change
- closed segments are immutable; no in-place rewrite is allowed
- projectors and rebuild tools consume closed segments in lexicographic order, then the active segment tail when present

- redb projections, JSONL mirror files, and Tantivy indices are rebuildable from seglog plus stable checkpoints; none of them outrank seglog as authority
- on restart, replay begins from the last committed checkpoint `{ segment_generation, segment_name, byte_offset, last_seq }`
- if the active segment ends with a partial/corrupt tail, rebuild truncates only after the last verified record and records the recovery action
- rebuild MUST preserve `sequence_id` ordering; regenerated mirrors or indices may differ in file timestamps but not in semantic event order

- Seglog is the authoritative append-only store for persisted `EventRecord` values. The seglog record payload is the MessagePack-encoded EventRecord envelope; JSON/JSONL mirrors are diagnostics and exports only.

- The seglog header may duplicate `event_type`, `sequence_id`, source/observed timestamps, and payload length for scanning and corruption recovery, but the decoded EventRecord value remains the semantic record.

- Physical append identity is `{segment_generation, segment_name, byte_offset, sequence_id, event_id}`. Replay order is segment generation, segment lexical order, byte offset, and `sequence_id`; timestamps never reorder replay.

- redb MUST NOT become a second mutable event source of truth. redb may store checkpoints, projections, idempotency indexes, and lookup rows keyed as `event_record_index.v1:{project_id}:{sequence_id}:{event_id}` with value `{schema_id, schema_version, event_type, segment_ref, byte_offset, payload_sha256, idempotency_key, correlation_id, causation_event_id?, persisted_at_utc}`. These rows point back to seglog and are rebuildable.

- `schema_version` is part of the durable value, projector checkpoint, and redb lookup value. Projectors MUST reject a record whose `schema_id` or `schema_version` is unsupported rather than inferring a shape from `event_type`.

- `payload_schema_id` dispatches concrete event-type payload validation. `Contracts_V0.md` owns the envelope; storage-plan owns payload schema registration, replay, retention, and projection storage mechanics; producer docs own event semantics. Until a concrete payload schema exists for a given event family, that family is not materially complete.

- Replay and idempotency use `event_id`, `idempotency_key`, `sequence_id`, and `replay_policy`. Duplicate delivery returns the original append/projection result when `event_id` or `idempotency_key` matches the policy; timestamp equality is not a dedupe rule.

- Retention and compaction never rewrite closed seglog segments in place. Compaction may rebuild redb projections, lookup rows, JSONL mirrors, and Tantivy indexes; canonical EventRecord values are retained or migrated through append-only successor records plus governed retention/legal-hold policy.

- Raw secrets, tokens, passwords, credentials, API keys, OAuth values, local credential paths, and local machine secrets are invalid in EventRecord envelope or payload content. Secret-bearing operational data is represented only by non-secret refs governed by permission/account custody.

- This Tier 0C-1 boundary records partial closure for EventRecord persistence only. It does not claim `attempt_record`, `receipt`, `lane`, `worktree`, provider stream, runtime lifecycle, clean-room harness, GUI, security, behavioral acceptance, or all redb value schemas are complete.

Regex-index compression and metadata policy: each posting list is a Roaring Bitmap (`roaring` crate) over `u32` file IDs, highly compressed for dense and sparse sets, and supports fast intersection/union (`/union`) for multi-n-gram queries. `index_meta.json` carries `anchor_sha: string | null` (Git HEAD SHA, null for non-Git), `build_timestamp_utc` as ISO-8601 with Z, `schema_version: u32` starting at 1 and incremented on format-breaking changes, `file_count: u32`, `generation: u64`, `case_sensitive_fs: bool`, `roaring_format: "portable"`, and `checksums` as per-file xxh3 hex strings exactly shaped `{ "file_map": "<hex>", "lookup": "<hex>", "postings": "<hex>" }`. Dirty file lists are in-memory only per `/Q19`.

- **`index_meta.json`:** metadata object with these required fields: `anchor_sha: string | null`, `build_timestamp_utc: string`, `schema_version: u32`, `file_count: u32`, `generation: u64`, `checksums: { file_map, lookup, postings }`, `case_sensitive_fs: bool`, and `roaring_format: "portable"`. Dirty-layer state is NOT persisted in `index_meta.json`; it is reconstructed as needed because the index is a cache.
